description: (tikajs-u03v, Fixer D) Adapted from xberg (MIT) base64_tests.rs, which keeps the words of a plain sentence in a part labelled Content-Transfer-Encoding: base64. Tika 4.2.0 (oracle, PUT /tika/text, same bytes, filename a.eml) does not: it base64-decodes the part whatever it holds and the words are gone (it answers CJK/replacement characters). ripstream does the same, and this pins that it does not grow a keep-the-words fallback Tika lacks.
